name: Shebaniah
overview: Shebaniah was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as an Aaronic priest. He is specifically mentioned in the context of the sealed covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, highlighting his role in the religious leadership during the post-exilic period. His priestly service underscores his dedication to the worship and covenant faithfulness of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Shebaniah appears once in Scripture with no specific meaning or divine origin indicated. It is presented plainly as a proper name in Nehemiah 10:4.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Shebaniah was the son of Joseph, as inferred from Nehemiah 12:14. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Shebaniah's significance lies in his role as an Aaronic priest who participated in the solemn covenant renewal of the returned exiles. His inclusion among the signatories of the sealed document in Nehemiah 10 demonstrates his commitment to upholding God's law and leading the people in covenant faithfulness. This highlights the continuity of Levitical priestly service in restoring proper worship and obedience to God after the exile.
